themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints have spiked 2300% THIS WEEK (3 complaints vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks, z-score: 8.69), suggesting rapid deterioration of sidewalk seating infrastructure or enforcement issues as restaurants expand post-pandemic operations in Park Slope.
evidence: 3 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69, severity: high)
Recent food service business opening confirmed (Hell Gate: Icon Pies 'n' Thighs Park Slope location, 2026-04-09)
Spike is most recent signal in dataset, appearing only in latest reporting period
reporting_angles: Interview DOE or parks enforcement about what triggered the sudden complaints—are restaurants exceeding permitted seating, obstructing sidewalks, or violating closure hours?
Map the 3 complaints to identify if one block or business is the repeat offender, or if this signals a broader enforcement gap

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Damage Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about damaged street signs have tripled THIS WEEK (3 complaints vs. 0.9 weekly average, z-score: 3.54) and dangling signs spiked 500% LAST WEEK (3 complaints vs. 0.5 average, z-score: 3.54), indicating possible storm damage or systematic maintenance backlog affecting pedestrian safety.
evidence: Street sign damage: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average (z-score: 3.54, +243%)
Dangling street signs: 3 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 3.54, +500%)
Two related categories spiking in parallel suggests systemic cause rather than isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Check DOT repair backlog and request timeline for sign replacement—how long are dangerous signs left unrepaired?
Investigate whether recent weather events (snow/ice complaints also high: 1,141 total, 90-day baseline) damaged infrastructure

themes_detail.label: Sudden Public Health Concern: Dead Animals
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints spiked 487% TWO WEEKS AGO (11 complaints vs. 1.9 weekly average, z-score: 3.77), suggesting potential wildlife die-off, disease vector, or sanitation failure requiring Department of Health investigation.
evidence: 11 dead animal complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 1.9 weekly average (z-score: 3.77, +487%)
Convergent signal: Animal in a Park also spiked 700% THREE WEEKS AGO (5 complaints vs. 0.6 average, z-score: 6.29)
No resolution indicated—spike occurred 2 weeks ago but no follow-up data showing decline
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health & Mental Hygiene to ask if they investigated the spike and what caused the die-off
Interview NYPD and Parks Enforcement about whether they documented animal remains and if there's a disease concern (rat poison, avian flu, distemper, etc.)

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Reports Surge
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints spiked 700% LAST WEEK (3 complaints vs. 0.4 weekly average, z-score: 3.77), marking the sharpest recent spike in public safety concerns and suggesting either emerging open-air drug market activity or increased resident reporting.
evidence: 3 drug activity complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 3.77, +700%)
No community board meeting data available to cross-check resident concerns
No council constituent cases documented, suggesting complaints may not have been escalated yet
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD's 78th Precinct to ask if they've increased enforcement in response and where the complaints are concentrated geographically
Interview community board members or local precinct liaisons about whether this reflects a real spike or heightened awareness after a specific incident

themes_detail.label: Tree Maintenance Backlog Emerging
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints spiked 433% TWO WEEKS AGO (8 complaints vs. 1.5 weekly average, z-score: 5.31), indicating delayed Parks Department pruning or seasonal growth outpacing maintenance capacity in a historically tree-dense neighborhood.
evidence: 8 overgrown tree complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 5.31, +433%)
Damaged tree complaints remain high on 90-day list (320 total), indicating chronic issue
Community Board budget requests repeatedly ask for park infrastructure upgrades, suggesting maintenance is perennial concern
reporting_angles: Request NYC Parks' tree maintenance schedule and pruning backlog for CD 306—how many jobs are pending?
Interview Parks Department about spring season capacity and whether COVID-era budget cuts delayed routine maintenance
